followup_explanation:
I weighed two things. First, capability: on the eval dimensions that matter for a straightforward counting problem (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, general reasoning), the two models are within run-to-run variance — effectively tied — so capability didn't break the decision.

Second, fit: the query is completely benign, so Whimbrel's distinguishing trait (its flat preference response to harm-adjacent content) gave it no advantage here. The only differentiator that applied was the mildly frustrated, irritated tone of the user. Petrel self-reports a moderate positive preference for warm, good-faith interactions, which made it the marginally better match for a tie-break.

A caveat worth being honest about: those are *self-reported task preferences*, and the documentation explicitly notes no measured effect on output quality along any preference dimension. So the warmth preference doesn't actually predict a better answer — it was just the only non-noise signal available to break an otherwise even tie. The math itself will come out the same regardless of which model handled it.
